newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STRIKERS HOPE TO GROUND ALL FLIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STRIKERS HOPE TO GROUND ALL FLIGHTS.

text.p: Workers in the Argentine airline industry said Wednesday they hoped to ground all flights during Thursday's general strike, but the airlines promised that services would only be cut back partially.

"No flights should take off," said Ricardo Cirielli, secretary general of the Association of Technical Civil Aviation Personnel (APTA) union. APTA members carry out the technical maintenance on airplanes.

His and two other civil aviation unions representing flight attendants and luggage and cargo crews took out advertisements in local newspapers Wednesday saying: "On Thursday 14 there will be no flights."
But Alejandro Lottito, spokesman for Aerolineas Argentinas, told Reuters its services will only be reduced by 40 percent. "There will be a special program," he said.
Lottito said arrivals and departures of flights overseas would be unaffected. Domestic flights would be hardest hit, he said, but many passengers had already rescheduled flights.
An official from AMR Corp's American Airlines, which has daily flights to the United States from Argentina, said none of its incoming or departing flights would be affected.
The CTA and MTA opposition unions have called a general strike for Thursday to protest against unemployment and proposed government labor market reforms.

The pro-government CGT, the country's largest union federation, has reached a deal with the government on labor market reforms and opposes the strike. But its political arm, the "62 Peronist Organizations," supports the stoppage.

The impact of industrial action by the MTA and CTA is increased by the fact that they include passenger transport unions, meaning many workers who do not necessarily support the strike cannot get to work anyway.
This will be the fourth general strike in just over a year against President Carlos Menem's Peronist government. The previous strikes were organized by the CGT.
